clue.text: Big Ben? Made a big noise, not half!

indicators.note: only half of the word survives here, the front half, since the clue asks for not the whole of it

parts.note: to make a big noise is to bellow, roared loudly, in the past tense

explanation.surface: A question about London's famous clock tower, followed by an exclamation about how loud it was, though only partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' keeps the first four of BELLOWED's eight letters. The question mark marks Big Ben as an example: it is the name of the great bell in the Westminster clock tower.
explanation.definitionFit: Big Ben is strictly the great hour bell inside the Westminster tower, an example of the class.

clue.text: Boyfriend appearing outside old city office

indicators.note: one piece is shown wrapping round the other, so the boyfriend word encloses the city

parts.note: a beau is an old-fashioned word for a boyfriend
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A suitor turns up around some ancient place to visit a workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A bureau is a government department or agency, a kind of office.

clue.text: Poet not allowed in the auditorium

indicators.note: an auditorium is where things are heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: something not allowed is barred, prohibited

explanation.surface: A poet has been banned from the concert hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A bard is a poet, especially an epic or lyric one; Shakespeare is the Bard.

clue.text: Characters with atrophy, sickness getting rare old medicine

indicators.note: the letters held within these two words, run together, give the answer

explanation.surface: Wasting and illness prompt a doctor to reach for an antique remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the end of 'atrophy' and the start of 'sickness'. 'rare' tells you the word is now seldom used.
explanation.definitionFit: Physic is an archaic word for medicine or a medicinal drug, still seen in older texts.

clue.text: Organic compound that can be made from nice oils

indicators.note: the letters of these words are reworked to produce something new from them

explanation.surface: A chemistry lesson on a substance produced from pleasant oils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made from' asks you to rearrange NICE OILS.
explanation.definitionFit: Silicones are synthetic polymers with organic groups attached to a silicon-oxygen chain.

clue.text: Psychiatrist here again? Cringe

parts.note: shrink is informal slang for a psychiatrist, from headshrinker
someone here again is back, returned

explanation.surface: A patient flinches on seeing their psychiatrist return.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrink back is to recoil or flinch away in fear or embarrassment.

clue.text: Urbane MP in new deal that's a bit shady

definitions.note: an adjective phrase standing for a noun: the partly shaded region

indicators.note: a fresh deal of the cards reorders them, so these letters are shuffled anew

explanation.surface: A suave politician mixed up in a fresh arrangement that seems a little dodgy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new deal' rearranges URBANE MP. 'a bit shady' reads as dishonest, but it means partly in shadow.
explanation.definitionFit: The penumbra is the partial shadow at the edge of a full shadow, as in an eclipse.

clue.text: Kitchen item available from book library maybe!

parts.note: a library is one example of a lender, as it loans books

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget you can borrow from a book library.
explanation.definitionFit: A blender is an electric appliance for liquidising and mixing food.

clue.text: Hot number getting top position perhaps

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
eight is a number

explanation.surface: A popular performer gains the highest place in the charts.
explanation.definitionFit: A height is a high point or summit, so the top position is an example.

clue.text: Say, member is drowning in beer!

indicators.note: something drowning is surrounded by the liquid, so one piece sits inside the beer word

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
a leg is a limb, which is a member of the body

explanation.surface: Someone claims a person is sinking into their drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to claim or assert something, typically without proof.

clue.text: Drip is getting worse and it brings dismay

indicators.note: something getting worse is deteriorating, so these letters break down and re-form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A leak gets worse and causes despair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting worse' rearranges DRIP IS into DISPIR, and IT is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispirit is to make someone lose heart or enthusiasm, discouraging them.

clue.text: Never stopping as revolutions go on

explanation.definitionFit: Round-the-clock means continuously day and night, and also describes the hands sweeping full circles of a dial.

clue.text: Agent with strange dialect gets copied

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent

indicators.note: the word dialect is made strange, its letters put in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A sales rep with an odd accent is imitated.
explanation.definitionFit: Something replicated is reproduced exactly, a duplicate or facsimile.

clue.text: Beautiful female as captured by the lens

indicators.note: the run of letters is caught within these words, running across the gap

explanation.surface: A lovely woman photographed through a camera.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'the' and 'lens'. Helen of Troy, in Greek legend, was the most beautiful woman in the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Helen of Troy is the legendary beauty whose abduction started the Trojan War.

clue.text: Wartime food plans put back

indicators.note: putting the word back turns it end to end so it reads in the other direction

parts.note: maps are plans or charts, as in mapping something out

explanation.surface: Food planning is delayed during the war.
explanation.walkthrough: SPAM, a tinned pork product, was a staple of the British wartime diet under rationing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinned luncheon meat was shipped widely to Britain under Second World War rationing.

clue.text: The most important course? Mum's in agreement

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mum; the 's stands for is, a link
being in line means being in accord or agreement

explanation.surface: Mother agrees on what the main dish of the meal should be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests a meal, but here it means a route: the main line of a railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A main line is the principal railway route, the chief track between major stations.

clue.text: Car goes on wheels

explanation.surface: A motor vehicle travels on its tyres.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rolls-Royce is a luxury motor, often just called a Rolls; something going on wheels moves by turning over and over.

clue.text: Pupil going off in car — hols!

indicators.note: something going off goes bad or explodes, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A schoolchild leaves on holiday in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going off' rearranges CAR and HOLS; hols is British slang for holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a pupil or student, especially a learned one at school.

clue.text: Dairy product manufactured the wrong way

indicators.note: reading a word the wrong way means taking its letters from right to left

parts.note: manufactured means made

explanation.surface: A milk product has been produced incorrectly.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a mild Dutch cheese with a red wax coating, a dairy food.

clue.text: Birthday bonus that's nice but superficial?

definitions.text: Birthday bonus that's nice but superficial?

parts.words: Birthday bonus that's nice but superficial?
parts.note: an extra treat that is pleasant yet merely added on top, like the frosting on a party sponge

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means an extra advantage on top of something already good, from the frosting laid on a birthday sponge.

clue.text: River foremen abandoning river

indicators.note: the foremen give up, leaving behind the letter for river

parts.note: a ganger is the foreman of a gang of labourers

explanation.surface: A river where the overseers have deserted their stream.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ganges is the great sacred river of northern India and Bangladesh.

clue.text: Warning when tiger's seen round the road?

indicators.note: the tiger goes round the road, enclosing it

parts.note: a tiger is a big cat
Ave is the abbreviation for avenue, a road

explanation.surface: A caution issued when a tiger is spotted near the highway.
explanation.definitionFit: A caveat is a caution or proviso, from the Latin for let him beware.

clue.text: Heather invading weakens young trees

indicators.note: the heather pushes its way into the weakens word, sitting inside it

parts.note: to sap is to weaken or drain
ling is a name for common heather

explanation.surface: Heather spreading into a plantation is undermining the young trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Saplings are young trees, especially ones with slender trunks.

clue.text: Wise man not finishing a long account

indicators.note: the wise man does not finish, so his final letter is lost

parts.note: a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: A philosopher who cannot complete a lengthy story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finishing' drops the last letter of SAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long story or narrative, originally a Norse heroic tale.

clue.text: Light-heartedness of priest starts to trouble you

parts.note: Levi was the founder of the Levites, the priestly tribe of Israel

indicators.note: the opening letters of the next two words are taken

explanation.surface: A clergyman's cheerfulness begins to bother you.
explanation.definitionFit: Levity means frivolity or lack of seriousness, treating serious things lightly.

clue.text: The border he cut is neat

indicators.note: the word he is cut away from the word the, leaving one letter

parts.note: a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: A garden edge that a gardener has clipped looks tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The border' looks like one phrase, but 'The' is fodder: 'cut' trims it down to a lone T. 'neat' reads as a verdict on the hedge yet is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Trim as an adjective means tidy and in good order.

clue.text: Girl somersaulting in gym reveals feathery things

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: PE is physical education, the school gym lesson

indicators.note: a somersault turns a person head over heels, so her name is turned round

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl doing flips in the gym shows off her feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl' could be many names; the four-letter one that fits PE_ _ _ E is the usual crossword Anne, turned head over heels by 'somersaulting'. Pennae is a Latin plural, a word solvers may meet only in birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Pennae are contour feathers, the plural of the Latin penna, a feather.

clue.text: Like language from fellow turning hysterical

indicators.note: the fellow turns around, so his name reads backwards

parts.note: Reg is a man's name, used for any fellow
hysterical means wildly excited, manic

explanation.surface: A language like one used by a man who has become frantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses REG to give GER, followed by MANIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Germanic describes the language family including German, English and Dutch.
